clean: Dear all on award, I wanted to say thank you for the incredible work over the last month. We've had the highest admissions since January, and you've handled it with such patience. Few highlights. The discharge times have proved by an average of 40 minutes, the patient survey scored us 4.6 out of 5, and we didn't have a single complaint about food, which is a first. I also want to thank the volunteers, especially the ones who came in on New Year's Eve. They brought mince pies, which were gone in 10 minutes. The leaving drinks for Margaret are on Friday at 6 in the staff room. Please sign the card. And a reminder that the flu jabs are available all week. Usha

Hi Tom, it's Sou from the band. Thanks for confirming the booking for the 4th of December. I wanted to go over the technical stuff. We need a stage that's at least 4 meters by 3. We're a five-piece, so that's five monitors, two vocal mics, and a DI box for the bass. But we need a riser. The soundcheck needs to start at 5 because we've got a long set, around 90 minutes. We'd like two drink tickets each and a hot meal if possible. One of us is vegan, one is gluten-free, and the guitarist has a nut allergy. Please confirm that parking is free and the load-in is at ground level. Many thanks. So, yeah.

Book club notes for October. We met at the library on Thursday, eleven others. The book was the one about the lighthouse Peebre, and opinions were divided. Marta loved it, thought the ending was perfect, while then said it was too slow. And somewhere in the middle. The first half was great, the second half dry. We talked for about 45 minutes about whether the keeper was reliable, which led to a long argument about memory. Anyway, next month's book is the short story collection, 160 pages, so no excuses. I'll bring the biscuits, and we're meeting on the second Thursday, which is the 10th, in the small room because the big one is being painted.

Radio interview debrief. We did the breakfast show this morning. Halleck whispering on the questions about the album. I got a bit nervous and said the wrong release date. I said the 5th, it's actually the 15th. They might correct it on air. The host asked about our influences, and I mentioned three bands. I should have said four. I forgot the one we all love. The interview ran 7 minutes instead of the planned 5, which is a good sign. They played our single twice, and the producer said she'd have us back in the spring. We should follow up with a thank you note and post the clip on our channels. I'll ask the station for the link.

Committee summary after the match. We discussed the new sponsor, a local dentist, offering £4,000 for the shirt front. The vote was 7-2 in favour, and the logo needs approval from the league. I'll send the paperwork on Monday. The treasurer says the floodlight fund is at £11,000. The committee agreed three things.
1. We apply for the grant to replace the floodlights. Dennis is drafting that.
2. We move the youth training to Wednesdays because the pitch is free.
3. We keep the ticket price at £8 for...

So we're here with a recap of the training day. Thank you to everyone who came. We had 33 people, which is great for a Monday. The morning session on manual handling went well but ran over by 15 minutes. The afternoon session on the new electronic records system was more chaotic. The logging kept failing for about 10 of it, so it came and reset the passwords. If you still can't get in, please raise a ticket and don't just keep trying because it locks you out after three attempts. The certificates will be emailed by Friday. If you didn't sign the attendance sheet, let me know. I also found a phone charger and a lanyard. They're in the office. And finally, the next training is on the 16th. It's about infection control, which is mandatory.

Dear friends and family, you're warmly invited to celebrate my father's 80th birthday. It will be held at the town hall on Saturday the 2nd of August from 12:30. Lunch will be served at 1:15. There will be speeches at around 3, so if you'd like to say a few words, please let me know in advance. No gifts please, but if you'd like to give something, he's collecting for the local hospice. We've booked rooms at the inn next door for those travelling. Please ask for the family rate. Please RSVP by the 20th of June to my email, pearson.hale@example.com. We look forward to seeing you. Carmen

Proposed changes to the constitution. Section 4, membership. Anyone over 16 may join, with parental consent required for those under 18. The annual fee is set by the committee and must be paid by the 31st of August. Members who fail to pay will lose voting rights, but they can rejoin at any time by paying the outstanding amount. Section 5. The annual general meeting is held in September, and a quorum is 20 members or 10% of the membership, whichever is lower. Notice must be given at least 21 days in advance. Section 6, the committee. It consists of a chair, a secretary, a treasurer, and up to four ordinary members, each elected for two years. Chianu has agreed to take the minutes until the next election.

You will not believe what happened at the party. We're all in the garden, and the cake comes out, and Agnes is about to blow out the candles when the dog, the neighbour's dog, jumps the fence and goes straight for the cake, face first. There's frosting everywhere. The kids are screaming. One of them is crying because he thinks the dog is hurt. The dog is obviously fine, he's just very happy. We managed to save about half the cake, we cut off the bit he'd touched, and we all had a slice anyway. Agnes laughed so hard she cried. I got the whole thing on video. I'll send it to you. It's the best thing, you love it.

Merch report for the autumn tour. Total sales were £6,240, which is up 18% on spring. T-shirts were the biggest seller at about 40% of revenue, followed by vinyl at 31%. Hoodies were disappointing, only 12%, I think because we only had them in black. The profit margin overall is 55% after the printer's costs. Card payments were about 70% of sales, and the card reader failed twice in Glasgow, so we lost maybe £200. I'd like to buy a backup reader. They cost about £70. And I'd also like to order the hoodies in gray and green for the next month. Commitment

Winter plan for the allotment. The beds are the main job. We're going to clear all the summer crops by the end of October, then add a layer of compost about 5 centimeters deep and cover it with cardboard to suppress the weeds. The garlic and broad beans go in during November. Caleb is ordering the bulbs. We want about 240. As for the tools, everything gets cleaned and oiled before it goes into the shed. I'd like to do a work day on the second Sunday of November for that. The water is next. We turn off the standpipe on the 1st of November to avoid frost damage and drain the butts. And finally, the greenhouse needs new glass in two panes. It's about £30. I'll sort it.

Just an update on the shed project. The base is done. The concrete went down on Wednesday, and it's been curing since. We'll build the frame this Saturday if the weather holds. I've got the timber coming at 9. It's about £210 for the lot. Kenny's brother has offered to help with the roof. He's a roofer, so that should be quick. The plan is to finish by the end of next week. We need four volunteers on Saturday and someone with a drill. I've got one, but the battery is flat, so if you've got a charger that fits a yellow drill, bring it. And please bring your own lunch. I'll supply tea and biscuits.

Dear Mr Thomson, I'm writing about the order we placed on the 3rd of September for 60 replica shirts, order number 8472. We were told delivery would be within 14 days. It's now been five weeks, and we still have nothing. I called twice and was told it would be shipped the following day, which didn't happen. Our season starts on the 12th, and our supporters have already paid, so this is urgent. Could you please confirm by the end of tomorrow when we can expect the shirts? If there's a problem, I'd rather know now. And if the order can't be fulfilled, we'll need a full refund of £1,800, to be processed within seven days. I look forward to your reply. Yours sincerely, Zoe

I've just been down to the site, and honestly it's a bit of a disaster. Somebody let the key open overnight, and the deer got in. They've eaten all of my lettuces, every single one, and half of the kill. It's not the end of the world, but it's a bit demoralizing, so I'd like to propose that we put a chain on the gate and a sign up. I'll buy the chain. It's only about £8. And I'd like us to agree who closes up on which days. I'm happy to do Mondays and Thursdays. The compost bay is also overflowing. We should talk to them about it. So if you've got any thoughts, please reply here.

Hi Mom, just a quick update on the house. I met with Carlos the mortgage broker this morning and he was really helpful. He says if we put down 15% we can get a rate of 5.25%, but if we manage 20% it drops to about 4.9%, which is a big difference over 30 years. He also said we should hold off signing anything until the appraisal comes back, which should be by the end of this week, and he wants copies of our last two years of tax returns, our pay stubs and the statements from the savings account. I'm going to scan everything tonight. Can you dig out the paperwork for the money Dad left me? I think it's in the blue folder in the hall closet. Thanks so much, love you, talk soon.

Just got out of urgent care and everything is fine, so don't panic. I know you're going to. I slipped on the ice outside the mailroom around 9 this morning and my wrist swelled up like a balloon, so Zara drove me. You remember Zara from my old job? She was amazing. We waited about 45 minutes, which honestly wasn't bad, and the doctor looked at it, sent me for an X-ray, and it turns out it's just a bad sprain, not a break, thank God. They wrapped it, gave me a sling I don't need, and told me to rest it for two weeks. The funny part is the nurse recognized me because she used to go to our church. Small world. Anyway, I'm going home to lie on the couch and feel sorry for myself. I'll call you later. Don't tell Mom until I've had a chance to talk to her myself.

Dear Ben, I hope you're well. I wanted to tell you about the tax thing before you hear it from Dad. I finally went to see Fiona, the tax preparer everyone at the office uses, and it turns out I've been filing wrong for three years, not wrong wrong, but I never claimed the home office deduction. She thinks I'm owed back about $2,400. She's going to file amended returns for me and it should take six to eight weeks. Her fee is about $250, which feels very fair. I'm telling you because you work from home too and you've probably done the same thing. You should give her a call. Her number is 555-0123, and tell her I sent you. Anyway, let me know how you're doing, and say hi to the kids. Your brother, Sam

Do the drive back from Leon's cabin was a disaster. We left at 1 because someone couldn't find his keys, I'm not naming names, and then about 40 miles in the car starts making this clicking sound, and we pull over, and it's a flat, obviously, and the spare is also flat, because of course it is. So we call roadside assistance and they say two hours, so we sit on the side of the highway eating gas station sandwiches, and honestly it was kind of fun. We played that dumb license plate game, and I won. But then the tow truck guy shows up and he's maybe 22, super nice, and fixes it in 10 minutes, so two hours of waiting for 10 minutes of work. Anyway, we got home at 10:30 and I'm still exhausted. We should do it again next month, but with working tires.

Dear Nadia, I know it's been ages and I'm sorry. Life has been, well, a lot. Since we last spoke I've moved twice, changed jobs once, and adopted a dog, a very large and very stubborn greyhound called Biscuit, who thinks the sofa is his personal property. The new job is at a small publishing house and editing cookbooks, which is funny because I can barely boil an egg, but I love it. We've got a book coming out in October about regional bread, and I've been eating a lot Pasado. I'd love to see you. Are you still in the sp a so I'm thinking of visiting in the spring, maybe April, and if not, wherever you are, I'll come find you. Write back when you can. With love, and apologies again, Lina

Hate me. I'm at the airport and the flight's been delayed again. They said three hours, which is ridiculous, so I'm sitting at gate 12 with a terrible coffee. Carlos is supposed to pick me up but I told him to wait until I text him, because I don't want him sitting in the cell phone lot for ages. I'll probably land around midnight, so don't wait up. There's leftover pop in the fridge if you're hungry, and the cat needs her medicine at 9. It's the little white pill in the cheese. Don't forget. Okay, love you, I'll see you tomorrow morning.

And I finally bought the car. I know you told me to wait until spring, but the dealer had a lightly used hatchback with only 22,000 miles on it and the price was $13,500, which is about three grand under what the others were asking, so I went for it. The unit came with me. She's better at negotiating than I am, and she got them to throw in winter tires and a free first service. It's blue, not the dark blue hate, more of a sky blue, and it has heated seats, which I know you think are a gimmick, but wait until you said and then in January. I'm going to bring it round on Sunday so you can have a look. Mom says she'll make the roast, and if you're going to tell me I made a mistake, please do it after dinner and not before. Thanks, love you.

The thing is, I think I need to tell you something about Mom. She called yesterday and she sounded really tired, and I asked if she was sleeping okay and she said she was fine, but then she mentioned that she's been getting up at 4 in the morning to water the garden because the heat is too much later, and that seems like a walk for someone her age. I was wondering if maybe you could go over this weekend too. I can't because I'm working Saturday and Sunday. Just see how she's doing, maybe take her out to lunch. She loves that diner on Route 9. I don't want to make a big deal. I just want someone to check. Please.

Hi Zara, thanks about Dad's retirement dinner. I've been looking at venues and I think we have three options. The first is the Italian place on Helm Street, which holds 40 people and is a private room. The second is the community hall at the golf club, which is cheaper but you have to bring your own food. The third is the back room at the pub where he's been drinking for 30 years, which I think he'd love, really love, but it only holds 25, so it depends who we invite. My vote is the pub, but I want to hear what you think. Also, the date. We said the 12th, but he has a doctor's appointment that morning, so let's make it the 19th. Can you ask Mun to check with his brother, and tell me by Thursday so I can put a deposit down? Thanks, talk soon.

Feels, I just saw Nina at the grocery store and she was totally ignoring me. She was literally looking right at me, and then she pretended to read the back of a cereal box, which is so awkward because we were fine last week. We went to that comedy show, so I don't know what happened. Maybe she's mad about the money thing. I did forget to pay her back for the tickets, it was 40 bucks. I'll then owe her tonight, but still, who hides behind cereal? Anyway, I'm gonna text her and act normal and see what she says. Wish me luck, lol.

Hey Martyr, I promised I'd tell you about the trip, so here goes. We landed in Lisbon on the 4th, it was raining sideways, and our hotel had lost the booking, which was fun, but they upgraded us to a suite, so no complaints. We did the tram to the castle, ate pastel de nata until we felt sick, took a day trip to Sintra where we got hopelessly lost in the gardens, and the last night we found this tiny place in Alfama with a woman singing fado, and I cried. I'm not ashamed, it was beautiful. You'd love it. We're thinking of going back in the autumn, and if you and Carlos wanted to come, we could split a house. It's cheaper than you'd think. Think about it, and I'll send photos when I've sorted them. There are about 400, so give me a week.

I finally told my boss on leaving. It went way better than I expected. She wasn't angry at all, she said she saw it coming, but she stumbled it, and she offered me a raise to stay, which honestly was tempting, but I've already signed the offer from the other place and I start on the 1st of March. It's less money at first but the team sings great and they let you work from home three days a week, which with the baby coming is a huge deal. Anyway, the last day here is the 27th of February, and they're doing a little lunch for me. I don't know why that makes me emotional. I've been here six years, and the thing I keep thinking about is how scary I was on my first day. I remember sitting in the car for 20 minutes before I could walk in, and now...

Dear all, here is the plan for the reunion in August. We have the lake house from the 9th to the 16th. There are six bedrooms, so couples get the rooms first and the kids can sleep in the loft. I'm assuming nobody minds sleeping bags. The cost per family is $450, which covers the rental, groceries and the boat fuel, and I'll collect it by the end of June. I need two volunteers to cook on the first night, someone to bring games, because last year there were none and the kids went forward, barrel, and one person to organize the photo. Uncle Roy has offered to be the photographer but only if we stop calling him the old man. I have promised nothing. The drive takes about five hours from the city, so leave early, and please tell me about allergies this week, not on arrival. Thanks, Fiona

Hi Leon, thanks again for offering to help with the move, I really appreciate it. Here's the plan so you know what you're signing up for. The truck is booked for Saturday morning at 8. It's 20 feet, because the guy at the rental place said 16 wouldn't fit the sofa. We'll start at the old place, then it's about 20 minutes by car to the new apartment on Harbor Street. The building has an elevator but it's small, so we'll have to take the sofa up the stairs, third floor, sorry about that. I'll buy pizza and beer afterwards, and I'll have all the boxes labeled by Friday night, I promise. If you can bring a hand truck that would be amazing, otherwise we'll manage. Let me know if anything changes. Cheers. And

We're thinking of doing the beach on Sunday, the whole crew, around 11. I'll bring the umbrella and the cooler. Nina said she'd do sandwiches, but she always forgets, so someone remind her. And bring sunscreen this time, because last time half of us looked like lobsters for a week. I'm looking at you. The forecast says it'll be 28 degrees and sunny, which is perfect, and we can stay till sunset if people want. There's a fire pit, we just need to bring wood. I think the permit is free, I'll check. And if anyone wants a ride, message me by Friday. I've got room for five in the Cardiffs, the kids squeeze. Okay, that's it, tell me.

Hi Mum and Dad, I have to tell you what happened at the bookstore today. I was shelving in the back and I found a box of donated books, mostly paperbacks nobody wants, but at the bottom there was a first edition of a novel by a very famous author, I won't say which. It had a signature inside, and my manager nearly fainted. She thinks it could be worth a couple of thousand dollars, so we're getting it appraised on Thursday, and the owner says if it sells I get a small bonus. Well, he said small. I'm hoping it's not that small. Obviously I'm trying not to get excited, but it's the most exciting thing that's ever happened at that shop. Ever happens there. I'll let you know how it goes. Love, Amara

Listen, I need your help with a surprise for Carlos. His birthday is the 2nd of November and he turns 40, so I'm renting out the back room at that toppest place he likes, for about 30 people. The guest list is nearly done. I just need you to get him there without him suspecting anything, so tell him you're taking him to dinner at 7, because everyone needs to be hidden by 7:15. Keep him busy for a bit, you could ask him about his bike or whatever, he never stops talking about it. I've already told his sister and the guys from the band. No one will say anything, And please don't post anything online, because he checks everything. I'll send you the address tomorrow. You're the best.

Mom, guess what, I got the job. It called me 20 minutes after I left. It's the hardware store on Fifth Street, assistant manager, and the pay is $19 an hour with benefits after 90 days. Andre the owner said he liked that I knew what a tavel bowl was, which is the dumbest reason to hire someone, but I'll take it. I start on Monday at 7, so I need to find my work boots. They're probably in your basement. If you can dig them out, I'll pick them up tomorrow. And can you tell Dad? He'll be happy. I'm still shaking a bit. I can't believe it. Anyway, call me when you get this.
